newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's preliminary Jan trade surplus $329 mln.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's preliminary Jan trade surplus $329 mln.

text.p: Mexico's preliminary January trade surplus was $329 million, with exports of $8.091 billion and imports of $7.762 billion, the Finance Ministry said on Monday.
The overall surplus was almost exactly the same as an average $328.8 million forecast in a Reuters survey of economists. Santander Investments predicted a trade surplus of $330 million.
The Finance Ministry said both import and export figures were lower than in the latter months of 1996, which it said was due to the timing of the first day of the month.

Manufactured exports were $6.591 billion, with maquiladora goods up 16.8 percent and non-maquila sales abroad up 7.1 percent. Petroleum exports were $1.069 billion, up 32.8 percent from Jan. 1996, with Mexican crude export prices $4.68 per barrel above its level in Jan. 1996. Crude export volumes were up 1.2 percent over the same period
Agricultural exports were $397 million, and mining sales abroad were $34 million.

On the import side, consumer goods reached $521 million, up 15.7 percent. Intermediate goods imports were $6.185 billion, up 18.1 percent, and purchases abroad of capital goods rose 34.2 percent to $1.056 billion.
